column1: # Where each woven Old English present participle in lex-ang.tsv was read.
# A verb row weaves its second form under an English -ing, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. Each modern verb form has
# named the table that prints it since 2026-10-08, and on the same day every
# woven Old English one was read in the rendered conjugation table
# (action=render) of its English Wiktionary entry: the cell classed
# pres|part, the present participle, quoted as the table prints it.
# tests/tools/ang-forms.test.ts fails on a form changed in one file and not
# the other, a line citing an entry its gloss was not read in, a quote from
# another cell or not printing its form, and a line outliving its row.
# A page holding more than one verb of a spelling is read by sense, as the
# plurals are: witan, to know, "witende", not wītan's "wītende".
# One entry per line, the one whose table the quote is from:
#                      (the title drops macrons and the dots of ċ and ġ)
# It is always an entry ang-glosses.tsv read the row's gloss in, so the two
# ledgers cannot choose different words of one spelling. Where the gloss was
# read in two, a ð spelling's page and the þ page it names, the line cites
# the one whose table prints the woven form as the pack spells it.
# Two things the pack writes otherwise than the tables, on every word, are
# read as one: ð, which the pack keeps where a teaching edition prints it and
# Wiktionary files under þ, and the doubled palatal, which the pack writes
# cg, "dg" in its pronunciation key, where the tables write ċġ.
# Laugh's was the headword's own mark. The pack wrote hlīehhan, and the
# table prints "hliehhende"; Wright § 69, read in the page image, prints
# "ea became ie (later i, y) by i-umlaut, as hliehhan (Goth. hlahjan), to
# laugh", the short diphthong, so the headword is hliehhan since 2026-10-09,
# its card following through RENAMED, and its line quotes the cell.
# 3 woven participles are not here, because the table prints another
# form: QUEUED in tests/tools/ang-forms.test.ts names each with what its
# table prints, until a grammar is read for it.
